001: Ivan, we have a problem with the supplier. They're delaying the shipment by a week.
Seriously? That could mess up our deadlines. What are we going to do?
I already called them. They offered to send half the order by plane.
That's a good option, but it's expensive. Let's calculate how much it will hit the budget.
I prepared the calculation. The difference is small if you take the late fees into account.
Then go ahead and agree. That way we'll at least keep our relationship with the client.
002: Dmitry, the client is complaining that we didn't account for one important requirement in the project.
That's strange, we signed all the documents. Maybe they changed the terms?
They say they sent us a letter with the changes, but we never received it.
I see. Let's check the email and the correspondence history to figure this out.
I already checked. The letter came in, but it went to spam, so we missed it.
That's unfortunate. Okay, we'll fix the project, but we'll ask the client to pay for the extra work.
003: Sergey, our server broke down, and some of the data might have been lost.
That's serious. Is there a backup? When was the last backup made?
There is a backup, but it's from yesterday evening. Some of today's work is lost.
Good thing it's not everything. Restore the data and tell the colleagues to check their files.
I'm already restoring it. But one report will have to be redone from scratch.
No big deal. The main thing is to find out why this happened and prevent it in the future.
004: Anna, we have a conflict in the team. Two employees can't agree on the approach to the task.
What exactly are they arguing about? Is it a technical issue or personal relations?
It's more technical. One wants to use a proven method, and the other wants a new tool.
Got it. Let's organize a meeting where each of them explains their position.
Okay. I'll gather them in an hour. Can you be there?
Yes, of course. We'll try to find a compromise so we don't slow down the work.
005: Ivan, we have a presentation for investors tomorrow, and the projector in the meeting room isn't working.
That's unfortunate. Did we call a technician? When can he come?
The technician said he'll only be here after lunch, but we need it by morning.
Then let's rent a projector from the neighboring office. I know they have a spare one.
Great idea. I'll call them and arrange to borrow it for a day.
Yes, and also check if there's a spare cable for the connection.
006: Dmitry, the marketing department sent a mockup, but there's a mistake in the product name.
Seriously? How could they miss that? We sent them the correct name.
Apparently, they used an old version of the brand book. I already wrote to them about it.
Good. Have them fix it today, since we're launching the ad campaign tomorrow.
They promised to send the corrected version by the evening.
Then once we get it, we'll all review it together so there are no surprises.
007: Sergey, we're running out of budget for this quarter, and the project isn't finished yet.
That's bad. How much are we short, and when do we need the money?
We're short about ten percent. We'll need to pay the bills as early as next week.
I understand. I'll talk to the financial director about reallocating funds.
That would be ideal. And if it doesn't work out, we'll have to cut back on the scope of work.
Let's first try to solve the money issue, and then we'll think about cutbacks.
008: Anna, the client is unhappy with our report and is demanding we completely redo it.
What exactly didn't he like? We did everything according to his technical specification.
He says we misinterpreted the data and the conclusions are wrong.
That's strange. Let's ask him to send specific comments so we can understand the essence of the complaints.
He promised to send his comments today. I'll forward them to you as soon as I get them.
Great. Then we'll go through them together and decide what really needs to be fixed.
009: Ivan, we have a logistics problem. The transport company lost part of the cargo.
That's really unpleasant. What exactly is missing, and how critical is it for the client?
A few boxes with spare parts are missing. The client is expecting them by the end of the week.
We need to contact the transport company right away and demand compensation.
I already sent them a claim. They promised to look into it within two days.
Good. In the meantime, let's think about how we can quickly deliver the spare parts another way.
010: Dmitry, an employee from our department is going on vacation, and nobody took over his tasks.
Didn't we distribute his duties in advance? This is a planned vacation.
Yes, but he was supposed to hand things over, and he got sick and didn't manage to finish everything.
I see. Then we need to split his tasks among the rest of the team right away.
I already made a list of tasks and sent it to the colleagues. They agreed to help.
Great. Then gather everyone for a short meeting to discuss the details and deadlines.
